payload.title: [auth-saml-2] Malformed NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter silently skips the validity-window check (Date.parse NaN)
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-saml-2 (medium/correctness, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/saml.ts
LINES: 319-333, 368-379

WHAT: All four time comparisons use Date.parse() raw: `now+skew < Date.parse(nb)` (319), `now-skew >= Date.parse(noa)` (327), `now-skew >= Date.parse(scNotOnOrAfter)` (370), and `Date.parse(scNotOnOrAfter) < Date.parse(notOnOrAfter)` (377). For an unparseable timestamp Date.parse returns NaN, and every relational comparison with NaN is false, so the bound is silently treated as satisfied. Empirically confirmed: an assertion with `NotOnOrAfter="not-a-date"` (NotBefore valid, well past intended expiry) is ACCEPTED, and an assertion with `NotBefore="garbage"` is accepted regardless of how far in the future it claims to start. The garbage string is then returned as verified.notOnOrAfter.

IMPACT: The Conditions validity window — a core freshness control — can be disabled by a malformed timestamp. The value lives inside the signed assertion, so this is primarily an IdP-bug / defense-in-depth exposure (a signed assertion with a malformed expiry never expires on Conditions grounds), and it pollutes the replay store's expires_at (see auth-saml-4). Not a direct unauthenticated attacker bypass, but it removes a guarantee the module advertises as 'non-negotiable'.

SUGGESTED FIX: Parse each timestamp once into a number and reject the assertion (SamlValidationError) when Number.isNaN(parsed) for any present NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter. Treat an unparseable freshness bound as a hard failure rather than an absent constraint.
